name: Should I add AI discovery files to my existing website or build a separate AI resource library?

mainEntity.name: Should I add AI discovery files to my existing website or build a separate AI resource library?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Google does not require a new AI file, special markup, or separate AI-only website for visibility in its search features. A dedicated resource library can still be useful when it improves organization, crawlability, and coverage without creating duplicate or low-value pages.

Context: AI Visibility Solutions uses a separate static library to hold answer-first FAQs and help articles while linking them to the primary business identity. The decision depends on the site’s current CMS, technical limitations, editorial workflow, and canonical strategy.

Key factors:
- Whether the existing site can publish fast, accessible HTML.
- Whether a second property would confuse users or search engines.
- How updates and approvals will be managed.
- Whether every resource has a clear purpose and owner.

Practical guidance: First test improvements on the main domain. Choose a separate library only when it solves a documented publishing or performance problem and can be maintained consistently.

Architecture should serve clarity, not create extra infrastructure for its own sake.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use the existing website when it can publish crawlable, useful HTML efficiently. Consider a separate library only for a documented technical or publishing need, with clear ownership, canonical relationships, consistent branding, and a maintenance plan.
